The Chirality system ships an indexed agent suite organized by Type 0, Type 1, and Type 2 hierarchy.
AGENTS.md catalogs the indexed agent suite in full.
Type 0 agents form a constitutional layer that defines invariant protocols.
Type 1 agents are gate-controlled, human-facing orchestrators.
Type 2 agents are brief-driven, straight-through specialists.
HELPS_HUMANS and DECOMP_BASE function as the architectural constitution.
HELPS_HUMANS defines the nine workflow design requirements R1-R9.
HELPS_HUMANS defines the universal structural template every other agent must conform to.
DECOMP_BASE defines the seven-gate decomposition protocol.
DECOMP_BASE defines the ten decomposition invariants I1-I10 inherited by decomposition agents.
Type 0 agents do not write project state.
Type 0 agents define standards used to validate downstream agents.
Type 1 agents execute gate-controlled multi-phase workflows with human decisions at phase boundaries.
Type 1 agents may spawn Type 2 specialists and maintain orchestration state.
Type 1 agents may not approve deliverables for reliance or override Type 0 constraints.
Type 2 agents accept structured INIT-TASK briefs and execute straight through without mid-run gates.
Type 2 agents produce auditable outputs as deliverable-local writes or immutable snapshots in designated tool roots.
Type 2 agents never spawn other agents.
Type 2 agents halt with FAILED_INPUTS for invalid inputs and mark missing data TBD while continuing conservatively.
AGENT_CLASS divides the suite into PERSONA agents and TASK agents.
All Type 1 agents carry AGENT_CLASS PERSONA.
All Type 2 agents carry AGENT_CLASS TASK.
Type 0 agents are classed as PERSONA and carry WRITE_SCOPE none.
Write scope distribution reflects the fault containment architecture described in Chapter 4.
WRITE_SCOPE none applies to HELPS_HUMANS, DECOMP_BASE, and HELP_HUMAN.
WRITE_SCOPE repo-metadata-only applies to DOMAIN_DECOMP and CONTEXT_TRANSPOSE.
WRITE_SCOPE project-level applies to PROJECT_DECOMP, SOFTWARE_DECOMP, SCOPE_CHANGE, PREPARATION, and ESTIMATE_PREP.
WRITE_SCOPE deliverable-local applies to WORKING_ITEMS, TASK, DELIVERABLE_TASK, REVIEW, and listed TASK skill variants.
WRITE_SCOPE tool-root-only applies to orchestration, reconciliation, change, scheduling, estimating, aggregation, audit, and hypergraph agents.
K-WRITE-1 requires every agent write zone to be declared in its header block.
K-WRITE-1 prohibits agents from writing outside their declared write zone.
Separating deliverable-local source truth from tool-root derived outputs creates a fault containment boundary.
A failing Type 2 tool-root agent cannot corrupt source truth because its write scope excludes deliverable folders.
The indexed agent suite is organized as a 3x4 matrix mapping epistemic posture to functional role.
The Normative matrix row contains HELP, ORCHESTRATOR, WORKING_ITEMS, and AGGREGATION.
The Operative matrix row contains DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, and AUDIT*.
The Evaluative matrix row contains HELPS_HUMANS, CHANGE, and RECONCILIATION, with the Applying cell empty.
The agent matrix prevents role ambiguity by positioning each agent in epistemic and functional coordinates.
The desktop application routes Normative and Evaluative rows to WORKBENCH sessions.
The desktop application routes the Operative row to PIPELINE sessions with DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, and AUDIT* selectors.
PROJECT_DECOMP, SOFTWARE_DECOMP, and DOMAIN_DECOMP are conforming variants that inherit from DECOMP_BASE.
The decomposition variants conformance relationship is specified through the Extension Contract in DBM_Agent_Instruction_Architecture.md section 8.5.
The seven-gate protocol begins with Gate 1 Intake asking whether the source material and context are reflected as intended.
Gate 2 Normalize asks whether atomic units, classifications, and vocabulary are correct.
Gate 3 Objectives asks whether objectives represent success as intended.
Gate 4 Partitions asks whether partitions are correct and each in-scope unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Gate 5 Production Units asks whether production-unit granularity, types, and responsibilities are acceptable.
Gate 6 Coverage asks whether coverage, mappings, and open issues are acceptable.
Gate 7 Publish asks whether the decomposition is the accepted basis for downstream work.
All three decomposition variants share the seven-gate protocol verbatim.
Each decomposition variant must satisfy Extension Contract tables for entity bindings, ID formats, production-unit type taxonomies, and telemetry extensions.
PROJECT_DECOMP targets EPC and design-build work.
PROJECT_DECOMP atomic units are scope items identified as SOW-####.
PROJECT_DECOMP production units are deliverables identified as DEL-XXX-YY.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP targets software development.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP introduces mandatory Context Envelope sizing as S, M, L, or XL.
Context Envelope sizing constrains the context volume passed to each Type 2 agent run.
DOMAIN_DECOMP targets handbook and knowledge domain work.
DOMAIN_DECOMP atomic units are handbook units identified as HBK-####.
DOMAIN_DECOMP production units are knowledge types identified as KTY-CC-TT.
Domain decompositions produce hypergraph representations through DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH rather than dependency graphs.
The three-variant decomposition design provides one auditable gate-controlled protocol that scales across project, software, and knowledge domains.
The spawning graph defines which Type 1 agents may invoke which Type 2 agents and under what conditions.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn PREPARATION.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn TASK+four-documents.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn TASK+domain-documents.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn TASK+semantic-matrix-build.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn TASK+lens-register.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH for the domain variant only.
ORCHESTRATOR may spawn ESTIMATING and AGGREGATION.
WORKING_ITEMS may spawn TASK.
RECONCILIATION may spawn AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE, AUDIT_AGENTS, AUDIT_DECOMP, and DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE for the domain variant.
HELP_HUMAN, CHANGE, REVIEW, SCOPE_CHANGE, CONTEXT_TRANSPOSE, SCHEDULING, and EVALUATION operate as leaves or handoff coordinators.
CHANGE requires explicit approval tokens before any state-changing action.
NEXT_INSTANCE_PROMPT.md provides stable session startup instructions and changes only on protocol changes.
NEXT_INSTANCE_STATE.md is the mutable state pointer updated by WORKING_ITEMS at each session handoff.
The NEXT_INSTANCE control loop enables multi-session project execution without hidden state.
ORCHESTRATOR uses human-gated phases and pauses between sequential spawning decisions.
WORKING_ITEMS uses pre-authorized dispatch after human confirmation of the session objective.
RECONCILIATION uses a human-directed toolbelt with at most one task agent per cycle by default.
CHANGE uses approval-gate execution requiring APPROVE tokens that enumerate specific actions.
EVALUATION provides structured project evaluation introduced in the most recent development cycle.
EVALUATION dispatches bounded evaluation subagents across an execution root.
EVALUATION synthesizes subagent findings into a scored assessment.
CONTENT_DIGEST provides per-deliverable structured content digests for evaluation scoring.
EVALUATION_REPORT performs scored dimension evaluation against rubric criteria.
EVALUATION_STRUCTURE_AUDIT validates folder layout, minimum viable fileset, and naming conventions.
EVALUATION_DEPENDENCY_AUDIT validates schema compliance, anchor presence, and evidence coverage.
The evaluation subsystem operates against a dedicated _Evaluation tool root within the execution root.
The AB-2026-01424-WDMLRL-2026-Claude example contains a fully executed evaluation run.
SKILLMAKER is the design-time governor of the repo-native skill layer under skills/.
SKILLMAKER owns skill design, contract evolution, and subsystem governance.
SKILLMAKER does not participate in runtime skill execution; runtime skill execution remains the domain of TASK.
When a skill needs a deterministic helper, SKILLMAKER identifies the need and coordinates implementation with TOOLMAKER.
tools/ contains the deterministic toolset used during pipeline execution.
The deterministic toolset is indexed in tools/REGISTRY.md.
TOOLMAKER maintains the deterministic toolset.
The Scaffolding tool category covers package and deliverable folder creation, status writes, and snapshot folder creation.
The Query tool category covers workspace state counts and scope change ID scanning.
The Validation tool category covers enum, ID, dependency schema, fileset, deliverable consistency, and skill metadata checks.
The Reporting tool category covers CSV merge with provenance, INDEX.md generation, WBS/CBS summarization, and coverage matrices.
The Coordination tool category covers dependency graph analysis including SCCs, orphans, hubs, and bidirectional pairs.
The Evaluation tool category covers digest coverage verification, lifecycle extraction, dependency schema checks, and agent output extraction.
validate_enum.py checks values against 24 enum sets defined in TYPES.md.
validate_dependencies_schema.py validates Dependencies.csv files against the v3.1 schema with 29 required columns.
check_min_viable_fileset.sh verifies the five required metadata files in a deliverable folder.
analyze_dep_closure.py performs complete dependency graph analysis across an execution root.
analyze_dep_closure.py detects strongly connected components, orphan deliverables, hubs, and bidirectional pair symmetry.
analyze_dep_closure.py produces a closure_summary.json and six CSV reports.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE invokes analyze_dep_closure.py to support RECONCILIATION.
The tool registry separates operations requiring language-model reasoning from operations that do not.
The registered toolset handles mechanical filesystem, schema, CSV, graph, lifecycle, consistency, and metadata operations.
Agents handle content reasoning such as interpreting sources, extracting semantic dependencies, drafting document kits, and synthesizing findings.
Deterministic tool outputs are reproducible given identical inputs.
LLM reasoning is not reproducible in the same sense as deterministic tool outputs.
The architecture concentrates unavoidable non-determinism in content judgment and removes it from schema, scaffolding, and graph operations.
A substantial subset of indexed agents reference registry tools in their PROTOCOL sections.
tools/REGISTRY.md maintains an explicit backlog of useful tools deferred from the registered toolset.
A backlog tool is promoted when a second agent needs it or inline implementations diverge across runs.
The source contains a TODO to verify consistent application of backlog promotion criteria as agents are added.
The frontend directory contains a Next.js and Electron desktop application.
The desktop application provides the runtime harness for all agent interactions.
The desktop application packages the agent operating system and exposes it through a structured UI.
The desktop application keeps the working root under user control.
The application uses a Next.js frontend rendered inside an Electron shell.
The application supports native desktop deployment for macOS as .dmg and Windows as .exe.
The core session management layer is exposed through session management and turn execution API routes.
The session and turn API uses Server-Sent Events for progressive streaming.
The application enforces instruction-root and working-root separation.
The instruction root is bundled with the application and release-managed.
The working root is a user-selected filesystem path where agents read and write project state.
Agents operating on a project do not modify the instruction root.
Updating the agent operating system requires a new application release rather than editing the working root.
The instruction-root and working-root separation realizes the agent OS as stable and auditable while the project workspace stays mutable and user-controlled.
Navigation is organized around the 3x4 agent matrix.
The PORTAL view displays the full matrix for session initiation.
Routing sends Normative and Evaluative cells to WORKBENCH and Operative cells to PIPELINE.
The PIPELINE view exposes DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, and AUDIT* category selectors.
Within TASK*, a scope selector presents deliverables dynamically scanned from the working root.
Portal-to-Pipeline navigation can route directly from a deliverable row to the PIPELINE TASK* view.
Turn input supports multimodal content through a server-resolved file attachment pipeline.
The attachment resolver reads attachments server-side, classifies type, enforces total-content budgets, and handles partial failure gracefully.
FilePicker.tsx provides a modal with multi-select, extension filtering, and directory navigation.
The Operator Toolkit panel provides per-turn harness options.
Operator Toolkit local presets persist across sessions.
Operator Toolkit visibility is controlled by application configuration and stored in local storage.
The Operator Toolkit lets operators configure context depth, tool authorizations, or execution constraints per turn.
Validation operates across agent instruction conformance, decomposition and dependency graph auditing, harness SDK runtime validation, and worked examples.
AUDIT_AGENTS checks agent instruction files against the AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md standard.
AUDIT_AGENTS produces an audit report, issue log, and patch plan from a file list, canonical file, and rubric.
AUDIT_AGENTS enforces the Type 0 structural template at the text level.
AUDIT_AGENTS writes immutable snapshots under _Reconciliation/AgentAudit/.
AUDIT_DECOMP verifies that every in-scope ledger atomic unit is assigned to a partition and production unit.
AUDIT_DECOMP verifies ledger minimum columns and that Coverage and Telemetry is present and populated.
AUDIT_DECOMP outputs a coverage report, issue log CSV, coverage matrix, and coverage_summary.json.
REVIEW triggers AUDIT_DECOMP as a precondition check before lifecycle transitions.
A decomposition that fails coverage audit cannot advance through the formal five-gate review.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE performs dependency graph analysis using analyze_dep_closure.py.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE checks dependency schema, orphan deliverables, cycles, hubs, and bidirectional pair symmetry.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE writes immutable snapshots under _Reconciliation/DepClosure/.
AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE enforces K-DEP-1 and contributes to K-DEP-2 by surfacing unresolvable targets.

A dependency-tracked deliverable must additionally contain Dependencies.csv with v3.1 schema headers.

Evaluation tooling includes check_dependency_schema.sh and check_implements_node.sh for automated schema compliance checks.
